items.h: Josh Cuevas is Best Left on the Waiver Wire For Now
items.s: Baltimore Ravens rookie tight end Josh Cuevas has been more involved in the offense in the past three games, hauling in eight passes on 10 targets. Cuevas has season stats totaling 119 receiving yards, which does lead the Ravens' tight end room, and one touchdown. While the increase in production is encouraging, he should be left on the waiver wire until he sees more on-field opportunity. He sits behind both veteran tight end Mark Andrews and rookie Matt Hibner in snap percentage, averaging only 29% over these past three games. In addition to Cuevas having a low snap percentage, the Ravens rank 28th in pass attempts per game at 28.9 attempts. This leaves little room for his production to…

Cuevas caught two of three targets for 35 yards during the Ravens' 35-13 loss to the Bengals on Sunday. Cuevas connected with Tyler Huntley on a 16-yard pass on the Ravens' offensive play of the game, but the duo didn't find each other again until late in the third quarter on a 19-yarder. Cuevas has only one catch for 14 yards through the first four games of the regular season, but the rookie fifth-rounder has an 8-105-1 receiving line on 10 targets over his last three outings. That coincides with Huntley being under center, but the Ravens are expecting Lamar Jackson (ankle) to return for Week 8 against the Bills on Nov. 1.

items.h: Rookie Josh Cuevas a Deep-League Tight End to Monitor
items.s: Baltimore Ravens rookie fifth-round tight end Josh Cuevas had his best day as a professional in the team's 13-10 loss on Sunday in Week 6 to the division-rival Cleveland Browns, catching four of his five targets for 44 yards and his first career touchdown reception. The 23-year-old from Alabama played the same number of offensive snaps (23 -- 40%) as fellow tight end Nick Vannett, with veteran Mark Andrews unsurprisingly playing 72% of the snaps. Cuevas has a total of seven receptions on only eight targets for 84 yards and a touchdown in his first six NFL games, but he has had multiple catches now in back-to-back games from backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. items.h: Josh Cuevas scores first TD in Week 6
items.s: Baltimore Ravens rookie tight end Josh Cuevas caught his first touchdown as a pro, the lone score for Baltimore in a 13-10 loss to Cleveland. Cuevas, a fifth-round pick in 2026, entered Week 6 with three receptions. He more than matched that production, recording four receptions and 44 yards on five targets, including a score. Veteran tight end Mark Andrews was quiet, and Cuevas stepped up. He is a player to monitor in dynasty formats.

Cuevas caught four of five targets for 44 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 13-10 loss to Cleveland. Cuevas got the scoring started Sunday, reeling in a two-yard score from quarterback Tyler Huntley in the first quarter. The touchdown was the first of his career, and he finished tied for second on the team in both targets and catches in Week 6. Cuevas has now reeled in multiple passes in consecutive games, but he will continue to be hard to count on from a fantasy perspective as long as starting tight end Mark Andrews is available.

Cuevas caught both his targets for 15 yards in Friday's 41-3 preseason win over the Commanders. Veterans Mark Andrews and Durham Smythe once again were kept off the field, leaving Cuevas and fellow rookie Matthew Hibner to handle most of the tight end duties. Cuevas, a fifth-round pick out of Alabama, caught Tyler Huntley's first pass of the night before connecting with Joe Fagnano for a short gain in the second quarter. Neither young TE stood out in the exhibition finale, and their battle for the No. 3 spot on the depth chart could extend into the regular season.

Cuevas caught three passes on four targets for 46 yards during the Ravens' 13-3 preseason win over the Vikings on Saturday. Cuevas and fellow rookie Matthew Hibner were listed as the Ravens' starting tight ends while both Mark Andrews and Durham Smythe observed the game from the sidelines. Cuevas played a key role in the Ravens' first offensive series of the second quarter, hauling in passes of 23 and 17 yards from Tyler Huntley, with the drive ending with a 49-yard field goal from Tyler Loop. Cuevas is up to four catches on five targets for 57 yards across two preseason games as he competes against Hibner and Smythe for a consistent role in the Ravens' offense for the regular season.…

items.h: Josh Cuevas signs rookie deal with Ravens
items.s: The Ravens signed fourth-round TE Josh Cuevas to a four-year contract. Cuevas was a fifth-round pick of Baltimore earlier in April. He will be competing for a depth role in the Ravens tight end room.

items.h: Josh Cuevas selected No. 174 by Baltimore Ravens
items.s: The Baltimore Ravens have selected TE Josh Cuevas with the No. 174 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. The Baltimore Ravens lost two tight ends in free agency. While they address the loss of Isaiah Likely by drafting two big-body mid-round wide receivers, the Ravens still need to replace Charlie Kolar. Josh Cuevas will fill that void perfectly. Unfortunately, he won't have any meaningful fantasy value, even in the deepest of leagues.

The Ravens selected Cuevas in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, 173rd overall. The Ravens add another tight end to the mix after they picked up Matthew Hibner in the fourth round. They're likely hoping these additions stick after they lost tight ends Isaiah Likely (Giants) and Charlie Kolar (Chargers) in free agency. Cuevas spent the final two seasons of his five-year collegiate career at Alabama, working as a starter in 2025 and catching 37 passes for 411 yards and four touchdowns. At 6-foot-3, 245 pounds, Cuevas is a bit undersized, but he was a strong blocker in the SEC and could line up at fullback if needed in the NFL.
